beats.story: There will be questions. Ones I don't have socially acceptable answers for. I know because today is my birthday, and a last-minute meeting has appeared on my calendar. A poorly disguised office cake party will be my supposed reward for turning thirty-three six and a half hours ago. Half the office will cram around a conference table, against our will, to eat dry sheet cake and force polite smiles. The questions will be about my life and how I plan to celebrate. Answers: I don't have a life, and I will likely celebrate by drinking alone and going down Reddit rabbit holes researching random and upsetting things like fecal-matter transplants, or the Golden State Killer, while making myself regret everything. I'm not sure that's relatable, so I'll say I'm having dinner with friends.
beats.story_cn: 问题总会有的。那些我没法给出得体回答的问题。我知道的，因为今天是我的生日，而日程表里突然冒出个临时会议。一场伪装拙劣的办公室蛋糕派对，将成为我六个小时前迈入三十三岁的“奖赏”。半个办公室的人将违背自己的意愿挤在会议桌边，啃着干巴巴的盒装蛋糕，挤出礼貌的微笑。他们的问题会关于我的生活和庆祝计划。答案？我没有生活。我的庆祝方式很可能是独自喝酒，在Reddit的兔子洞里搜罗些稀奇古怪又令人不安的玩意儿——比如粪便移植，或者金州杀手——然后一边后悔人生。不确定这算不算共鸣，所以我还是说跟朋友吃晚饭吧。

beats.story: Oh, the lies I am forced to tell just to fit in at the western regional office of Supershops Incorporated. The meeting reminder flashes on my monitor again, persistent as a pesky cold sore. My fingers tingle, and I take a few slow breaths, but I can't get air to settle in my lungs. So many office situations show no regard for people with anxiety, yet we're the bad guys if we can't cope. I should just walk away from it all. My eyes dart to the flimsy wall of my cubicle where my name card still faintly reads Jolene Smith after years of sitting beneath violently fluorescent lighting. Three pushpins pierce the industrial fabric; they've always been there, even though I've never felt the urge to pin anything up. My workspace remains bare and beige in a sea of personalized cubicles.
beats.story_cn: 哦，为了在“超级商店有限公司”西区分公司合群，我不得不撒的谎啊。会议提醒再次在显示器上闪烁，顽固得像颗恼人的唇疮。我指尖发麻，深吸了几口气，却感觉空气滞留在肺外。多少职场情境从不顾虑焦虑症患者，可一旦我们无法应付，倒成了恶人。我真该一走了之。目光扫过格子间薄薄的隔板，我的名牌在荧光灯下常年暴晒，上面“乔琳·史密斯”的字迹已然模糊。三枚图钉扎在工业织物上；它们一直都在，尽管我从未兴起过钉点什么。在这片个性张扬的格子间海洋里，我的工位始终光秃秃，一片米黄。

beats.story: Yet those pins sit reassuringly in their same formation, day after day. And I don't think I could ever leave them. A new email appears in my inbox. It's from Rhonda, whose official title is "lead accounting administrator," but really she's just our boss Gregory's assistant, a role she's held for a thousand years. Reminder, I've booked you for a meeting in boardroom 435 that starts in one minute. You don't want to be late. This meeting has automatic reminders set up, yet she's emailing me from seven feet away. I peer over the half wall of my cubicle toward hers, which boasts a shelf lined with an assortment of dusty trinkets, inspirational quotes printed on crinkled yellow paper affixed to the wall, and a file box I know is filled with medications, tea bags, and biscuits that expired in 2012.
beats.story_cn: 然而那些图钉却日复一日，令人安心地停留在原处。我想我永远也不会动它们。收件箱里出现一封新邮件。是朗达发来的，她的正式头衔是“首席会计行政员”，但实际上只是我们老板格雷戈里的助理——她干这角色大概有上千年了。“提醒：我已为你预约一分钟后在435会议室开始的会议。别迟到。”这会议明明设了自动提醒，她却从七英尺外给我发邮件。我越过格子间的半截隔板望向她的工位，那里摆着一排蒙尘小摆件，墙上贴着皱黄纸印的励志名言，还有个文件盒——我知道里面塞满了药品、茶包和2012年就过期的饼干。

beats.story: It's as though she anticipates being trapped here one day and not only surviving the ordeal, but thriving. I don't mean to lock eyes with Rhonda; I blame her excessive eyeliner and the green eyeshadow that could direct traffic. She notices and breaks the stare first, lowering her head so I can see only the tips of her spiky grey hairdo. Then her mouse clicks, pointedly. Technically, she's to blame for this entire mess. She doesn't usually pay much attention to me, and when she does it's often paired with a scowl and a pointed gum-snap. But Rhonda runs the morale club, and with Brendan Fraser as my witness, there's nothing more demoralizing than the Morale Boosters. Her morbid obsession with birthday tracking, cake buying, and forcing people to sit through off-key renditions of the "Happy Birthday" song can't be out of love.
beats.story_cn: 她仿佛早已预料到有天会困在这里，不仅熬过难关，还能如鱼得水。我并非有意与朗达对视；要怪就怪她浓得能指挥交通的黑眼线和绿色眼影。她注意到了，率先移开视线，低头只让我瞥见灰白尖刺发型的发梢。接着她鼠标准狠地点了一下。说起来，这整场闹剧都该归咎于她。她平时不怎么理我，偶尔留意时也常配着皱眉和故意的咂嘴声。但朗达掌管着“士气俱乐部”，我以布兰登·弗雷泽的名义起誓，没有比“士气提振团”更挫伤士气的东西了。她对追踪生日、采购蛋糕、逼人听跑调版《生日快乐》歌的病态执着，绝不可能源于爱心。

beats.story: Planning these thirty-minute-long office parties and telling people about the mundane interactions she's had with service people are big portions of her personality, but her primary passion is her "grown-ass son," whom she visits every weekend. He's some rich dick who supports her. In her eyes, he is on the brink of curing all human ailments, keeps the transit running on time, and has about a million matches on Tinder. Although, judging by the framed picture of him on her desk, he could be the stock model used in advertisements for plain bread and mayo. I keep my expression deadpan as I turn back to my keyboard and type: Hello Rhonda, Thanks very much for reminding me about the meeting. I must say, your reminder is so much more personal and well received than the default one that the computer gives. I almost feel that one is pointless when I've got you in my corner. Best regards, Jolene Adding extra sugar to the part that's visible helps make the invisible part so much more satisfying.
beats.story_cn: 筹划半小时的办公室茶会、絮叨她与服务生的琐碎对话——这些虽构成她性格的重要切片，但头号热情所在仍是她那个"成人儿子"。她每周末都去探望，那是个养着她的有钱混账。在她眼里，此人简直站在攻克人类一切病痛的临界点上，能让公共交通分秒不差，还在Tinder上坐拥百万级匹配。不过从她桌上那张相框照片看，此君倒像极了白面包配蛋黄酱广告里用的平面模特。我面无表情转回键盘敲下：致罗达：多谢提醒会议。说实在的，你的提醒远比系统默认通知更贴心、更令人愉快。有你在侧，我都觉得电脑通知纯属多余。此致，乔琳（附：在可见部分多撒点糖，才能让暗处的蜜更沁人心脾。）

There are times, when you're on the phone fake laughing or retelling someone the same story about your toenail surgery, that make me consider joining a cult as a preferable alternative to staying here with you. I smile politely in her general direction. As I pass behind Caitlin's desk, the scent of the vanilla-icing hand cream she applies seventeen times daily wafts my way, microdosing my irritation. The same scent always transfers to the documents and envelopes she handles, like a dog marking her territory. She tilts her chin toward me and gives this little brow raise but doesn't look directly at me. Something uncertain bubbles in the pit of my chest. She's been watching me all day, and I trust her less than my Wish.com recommendations.

beats.story: Caitlin and I have worked adjacent to each other for three years in the same admin role. We were destined to be best friends, but because of who we are as people, our years of forced proximity have instead culminated in a specific form of petty hatred. The problem is Caitlin tries way too hard. She's still talking about how this job is a "jumping-off point" for her to step into a larger role at Supershops, while I gave up on that notion after less than a year here. Her violations include: cc'ing Gregory when she notices any of my errors "in case it becomes a relevant pattern" (which is a good point, and I've made sure to include him when calling out her mistakes too), forgetting to add my mug when she runs the dishwasher (I can never find space for hers either), and interrogating me when her yogurt goes missing from the office fridge (as if blueberry Dannon is something I'd mess with). It's reached a healthy point where our only communication is via curt emails, and we gleefully mix up anything the other sends to the printer. The room and the world compress in on me as the panel of shame stares me down. I nod stiffly. The only one to smile is Clifford. Gregory claps once. "Great." Anna pushes a small stack of papers secured with a binder clip across the table, then offers me a silver pen.
beats.story_cn: 四面八方都会响起嚼舌根的声音。但还不止于此。如果我不得不再次住在父母的屋檐下，这次真会要了我的命。当羞耻的审判团目光如炬地逼视我时，房间与整个世界向我挤压收缩。我僵硬地点了点头。唯一在笑的是克利福德。格雷戈里拍了一下手。“很好。”安娜把一小叠用活页夹固定的文件推过桌面，然后递给我一支银色钢笔。

beats.story: The cool pen is too heavy for my shaking fingers, but I manage to flip straight to the last page of the packet, which is marked by a Post-it flag, and sign on the line. Gregory and Anna shuffle out of their seats as Clifford waits behind me, collecting the documents. Gregory pauses and leans against the doorframe, his pants creased in all the wrong ways, his left hand very anchored in his pocket. "Clifford, you're going to have to set up Miss Smith's computer security today. Our IT service is on a work order. We'll show you the way." Then he marches out the door, Armin scurrying from his post at the printer in his wake. Oh my god. They're doing it now?
beats.story_cn: 冰凉的钢笔沉重得让我颤抖的手指几乎握不住，但我还是设法翻到了文件夹最后一页，那页用便利贴标记着，在横线上签了名。格雷戈里和安娜从座位上起身，而克利福德在我身后等着收拾文件。格雷戈里顿住脚步，斜靠在门框上，裤子皱得不成样子，左手深深地插在口袋里。“克利福德，你今天得设置好史密斯小姐的电脑安全权限。我们的IT部门正在处理一个工单。我们会给你带路。”说完他大步迈出房门，阿明匆匆忙忙从他的打印机岗位跟了上去。天哪。他们现在就要动手了？

beats.story: In front of everyone? My mouth sours, and Clifford, who is still arranging my paperwork, scrunches his shoulders guiltily toward me, which I don't buy. His whole career is shame centered. I peel myself out of the chair and head toward the exit, but my feet stop at the doorway, once again contemplating leaving for good and becoming a shepherd, or moving into a wax museum and pretending I'm a figurine. Clifford shifts the papers in his arms and says, "I noticed here that it's your birthday. Happy birthday! You're thirty-three. Same as me." I force a smile.
beats.story_cn: 当众宣布？我嘴里泛起一股酸涩，克莱夫还在整理我的文件，他心虚地朝我缩了缩肩膀——这戏码我可不信。他整个职业生涯都围着羞耻心打转。我把自己从椅子里拔出来，走向出口，却在门边停住脚步，又一次认真盘算着永久逃离职场，去当个牧羊人，或者搬进蜡像馆装成假人。克莱夫挪了挪怀里的文件堆：“我注意到今天是你生日。生日快乐！你三十三了，和我同岁。”我硬挤出个微笑。

beats.story: What is it with HR people always being so . . . in people's business? Like you have to be part sociopath to go into that line of work. "Thanks," I reply, and dryly add, "This is exactly how I pictured it." His laugh is way too loud, and I try not to encourage it with a smile. His notepad is tucked under his arm, and the doodle he was working on presses heavily into the page. "Nice cat," I say. "Glad you found the time for some artwork during my professional misconduct meeting." His mouth drops as his eyes slip away from mine. I'm out of the room before he looks up.
beats.story_cn: 人力资源部的人怎么总爱对别人的事指手画脚？好像非得带点精神变态特质才能干这行。“谢谢。”我应道，干巴巴地补了句，“正是我想象中的样子。”他的笑声震得我耳膜发疼，我努力不给任何鼓励的微笑。他的记事本夹在臂弯，刚才涂鸦的笔迹深深压进纸页。“猫画得不错，”我说，“很高兴你在我‘职业行为不端听证会’上还有空搞创作。”他嘴巴微张，视线从我脸上滑开。没等他抬头，我已夺门而出。
